description: Poles and zeros of a discrete-time system are dragged on the z-plane or set with radius and angle sliders. The magnitude and phase response are computed from the vectors between each pole or zero and a point on the unit circle, the impulse and step responses from the matching difference equation, and a banner reports whether the causal system is stable.

educational.topic: Pole-zero analysis of discrete-time systems in the z-plane
learningObjectives: Determine from a pole-zero plot whether a causal discrete-time system is stable
Explain the magnitude response as a ratio of distances from zeros and poles to a point on the unit circle
Relate the radius and angle of a pole pair to the decay rate and oscillation frequency of the impulse response
Design a simple resonator or notch by placing poles and zeros

controls.label: Remove
controls.description: Delete the selected pole or zero

controls.label: Click to select and drag poles and zeros on the z-plane; move the mouse over the magnitude or phase plot to set the frequency cursor

equations: |H(e^jw)| = product of distances from zeros to e^jw / product of distances from poles to e^jw
y[n] = sum_k b[k] x[n-k] - sum_{k>=1} a[k] y[n-k]
stable (causal, discrete time) if and only if every pole satisfies |p| < 1
assumptions: The system is causal and has real coefficients, so complex poles and zeros are kept in conjugate pairs
When the numbers of poles and zeros differ, zeros or poles at z = 0 make up the difference; they change the phase but not the magnitude
A simple pole on the unit circle is reported as marginally stable and a repeated one as unstable
The frequency axis runs from 0 to pi radians per sample; 50 samples of the impulse and step responses are shown

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Manipulate the pole-zero plot and link each move to the frequency response, the time response and the stability verdict
keyQuestions: Where must the poles of a causal discrete-time system lie for it to be stable?
Why does a pole near the unit circle produce a resonance peak?
What do the radius and the angle of a pole pair control in the impulse response?
commonMisconceptions: Zeros outside the unit circle make a system unstable
Stability in the z-plane means poles in the left half of the plane
A single complex pole can exist without its conjugate in a real system
assessmentOpportunities: Classify each preset as stable, marginally stable or unstable before loading it
Verify the magnitude at the resonance from the two pole distances
